subject: Private deployment addendum + evidence flow (sovereign hosting ask)
messages:
From: Matt Howard <matt.howard@healthsys.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T08:32:00-08:00
Subject: Private deployment addendum & evidencing for sovereign hosting

Diego,

Thanks for taking this call earlier. HealthSys needs a concrete path for a private (VPC/on‑prem) deployment that satisfies our regulator and procurement review. High level asks from our side: 

- License carveout for 'in‑scope production use' (we'd like to avoid broad rights).
- Operator access model: remote limited session, on‑site witnessing windows, and proof of operator actions.
- Audit/forensic access: periodic snapshots and an escrow‑style delivery if Redwood becomes unable to support the installation.
- Evidence package: runbooks, key rotation logs, KMS attestations, and a minimal forensic snapshot checklist.

Can you share an annex draft and an evidence matrix? Also let me know what you expect to be negotiated on the Order Form (dedicated capacity commit, pricing impact, and any required exhibits). Procurement copied.

Best,
Matt Howard
Director, Procurement — HealthSys Regional Health
procurement@healthsys.com

Attachments: evidence-request-outline.pdf (stub)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Matt Howard <matt.howard@healthsys.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment addendum & evidencing for sovereign hosting

Matt — thanks, very clear asks. Bringing legal & compliance into the thread so we can get targeted redlines. Proposed approach (quick summary):

1) Annex (MSA Addendum) draft: narrow license to "Production Use" with a specific exhibit listing allowed use cases and jurisdictions.
2) Evidence playbook: staged artifact delivery (initial onboarding binder, quarterly evidence snapshot, and a sealed snapshot for escrow scenarios).
3) Operator access: three tiers — remote console via bastion (audited), time‑boxed remote session with recording, and on‑site witness (by appointment). Scope operator credentials to a limited role; no root handover.
4) Audit / escrow: define trigger events for sealed snapshot release (bankruptcy, insolvency, failure to meet SLA X days). Keep delivery mechanism mutually agreed (SFTP + notarized hash).
5) Order Form impacts: likely a small premium for on‑site witness SLAs and evidence delivery windows; dedicated capacity is optional but recommended if you need predictable performance and a single‑tenant deployment.

I've attached an initial annex template (Private-Deployment-Annex_v0.1.docx) and an evidence matrix (evidence-matrix-healthsys.xlsx). Laura — can you run a first pass on legal redlines (scope, indemnity carveouts, escrow triggers and limits)? Neha / Rishi — any compliance/ops flags we should pre‑empt for HealthSys (data residency, key custody notes)?

If helpful I can schedule a 30‑minute legal & procurement sync early next week.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales Lead — Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415 555 0199

Attachments: Private-Deployment-Annex_v0.1.docx (draft annex), evidence-matrix-healthsys.xlsx (stub)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Matt Howard <matt.howard@healthsys.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment addendum & evidencing for sovereign hosting

Diego / team — I reviewed the draft annex and evidence matrix. High‑level redline guidance below and attached a redline PDF with comments. Key items we should negotiate from our side: 

- License scope: keep as "Production Use — Customer Internal Applications" and add an explicit prohibition on sublicensing or third‑party redistribution.
- Operator credentials: Redwood will provide operator sessions via a Bastion/Jump host only. Do not hand over permanent privileged credentials. Add a clause for recorded sessions and post‑session logs retained for 90 days.
- Escrow / sealed snapshot: limit triggers to insolvency, material breach with failure to cure X days, and court order. Cap the data and artifacts to what is strictly necessary to restore the service (no source code delivery).
- Audit windows: prefer remote access + artifact delivery over unrestricted on‑site for cost and security reasons. If on‑site is required, limit to scheduled windows and Redwood may charge reasonable travel/hosting costs.
- Liability / indemnity: reject any blanket customer right to seek source code; propose a narrowly tailored forensic artifact list and a mutual limitation on consequential damages.

I've added suggested language for an "Escrow‑Lite" exhibit that defines sealed snapshot format, notarized hash verification, and delivery mechanics. Also flagged encryption key custody expectations — HealthSys should define whether they require KMS bring‑your‑own‑key (BYOK) or Redwood KMS operations.

Next steps: I can produce a redline to the annex (attached) and an exhibit for the Order Form showing pricing uplift assumptions for on‑site witness and sealed snapshot management. Diego — if you can get procurement's maximum acceptable window for evidence delivery and whether they require BYOK, I'll finalize our positions for negotiation.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: redline-msa-annex_laura_bennett.pdf (redline + comments)

From: Matt Howard <matt.howard@healthsys.com>

Subject: Re: Private deployment addendum & evidencing for sovereign hosting

Diego / Laura — thanks for the quick replies. A few clarifications from procurement: 

- Pricing: HealthSys needs a line item for the "evidence & witness" service in the Order Form. We don't need source code; primary ask is the sealed snapshot + operator witness window. Please provide an estimate for one on‑site witness day and ongoing quarterly sealed snapshots.
- BYOK: regulator prefers customer‑managed keys (BYOK), but we can accept a managed key if Redwood provides KMS attestation and rotation logs.
- Escrow triggers: procurement prefers a low threshold (including failure to meet SLA for 60 consecutive days). Is that negotiable?

Also happy to take the 30‑minute sync. I'm available Tue 2026‑11‑17 09:00–10:30 PT.

Matt
Matt Howard
Director, Procurement — HealthSys Regional Health
